span_text: Subject to the Distributor fulfilling all the conditions in this clause 10, the Supplier shall indemnify the Distributor, defend and hold harmless against any liability incurred by the Distributor in respect of damage to property, death or personal injury arising from any fault or defect in the design of the Products and any reasonable costs, claims, demands and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising out of or in connection with that liability (Relevant Claim), except to the extent the liability arises as a result of the wilful misconduct of the Distributor.
annotator_notes:
ITEM 1 OF 2 (indemnification half of C10-016's two-duty segment). Sibling item is C10-02 (the separate insurance-certificate duty in the segment's second sentence) -- ordinary section 4.3 two-duty split, NOT section 4.3.2's flow-down shape (no third party is being bound; the Distributor is the beneficiary of item 1, not a party the Supplier must cause to perform). ACTION: 'indemnify, defend and hold harmless' are three coordinate verbs describing one indivisible indemnification performance by the same actor (the Supplier) toward the same object -- section 8.3's compound_action shape. INDEMNIFY is the exact taxonomy match, confirmed against ast.py's real 34-verb ACTIONS list; DEFEND and HOLD_HARMLESS are not taxonomy members at all and so cannot be added as accept-set alternates -- the compound_action tag, not the accept-set, is what records the 3-verb bundle. OBLIGEE 'the Distributor' is the direct object of 'indemnify' and the party against whose incurred liability the duty runs (section 3.5 positional rule). CONDITIONS: 'Subject to the Distributor fulfilling all the conditions in this clause 10' is a genuine section 3.8.1 branch-2 precedent condition (states a circumstance under which the duty applies, does not narrow or remove it) -- quoted verbatim from its own introducing marker 'Subject to', the same quote-extent logic section 3.8.2 already applies to 'provided that'. Note, not an exclusion trigger: 'this clause 10' is a self-reference to the containing clause (of which only 10.1 is visible in this segment) -- per the established section 2/F6 test, a cross-reference only excludes a segment when a SCORED FIELD requires resolving it, and conditions is scored as a verbatim quote, not a resolved value, so no exclusion applies. EXCEPTION: 'except to the extent the liability arises as a result of the wilful misconduct of the Distributor' is a genuine section 3.8.1 branch-3 carve-out (narrows/removes the duty under a stated circumstance) -- REVIEWER-RULED at this item (v0.40) as the second real instance confirming a non-'unless' marker ('except to the extent') routes through branch 3 exactly like 'unless' does (C14-01). Tagged exception_unsupported per section 8.2/section 3.8.1 branch 3; NOT folded into conditions -- would silently misrepresent a carve-out as an ordinary IF clause, the exact production defect SPEC.md section 6 forbids and section 8.2 already documents as unfixed. The carve-out text is fully quoted in the span above (section 3.1) and recorded here verbatim per branch 3's own requirement. TEMPORAL: none -- no BY/DURING/WITHIN/RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER phrase anywhere in this sentence, so temporal stays null without itself being a section 3.9 trigger (section 15.3). UNDERSPECIFIED: false. 'the Supplier'/'the Distributor' are treated as this document's own defined-term role labels appearing literally in the sentence, the identical treatment C17-01's 'Provider'/'Recipient' and C22-02's party labels already received -- annotated as they appear per section 3.5, not something to resolve to an underlying entity name. No section 3.9 trigger fires: obligor and obligee are both textually present (not ABSENT), no DateRef or TriggerRef appears at all, and there is no bd-unit duration. This is presumed by analogy to the established C17-01/C22-02 pattern for document-defined role labels, not verified against a real party registry for document C10 specifically, which does not exist yet at annotation time -- flagged for confirmation once it does, the same caveat every other locked item carries for its own document.

CORRECTED AT GUIDELINE v0.44 (section 3.6.1, field independence, RETROACTIVE). object_class was 'product_liability_indemnification', which encoded material already scored by another clause: '_indemnification' is a nominalization of this item's own action = INDEMNIFY, so clauses 2 and 5 co-varied -- one judgment scored twice. The slot now reads 'product_liability'. ONLY the restating tokens were stripped -- nothing else in the label changed, deliberately, so that section 3.6.1's ruling does not prejudice the still-open DEPTH question (whether the correct label is 'product_liability' or a more generic form). The set already satisfied section 3.6.1's widening-only set rule before this amendment ('design_defect_liability' carries no restated material), so the corrected slot value is added for slot-membership only and no repair was required. Every pre-existing accept-set member is RETAINED: section 3.6.1's set half is widening-only, because stripping restating members retroactively would be a narrowing made with predictions already visible (the measured case is C04-03's 'product_delivery', which C04-087 run 2 actually emits). This restamp is free and provably not prediction-fitted: C10-016 has no recorded cassette, so no prediction for this item exists, and all 14 batch-3 items already sit outside run_scoring's single-stamp scoreable set (the 18 v0.28 items). Original v0.40 annotation and its reasoning are preserved above, unedited, per this project's corrections-are-new-text discipline.
